messages:
Jordan: hey team — new hire here. quick q about tiny fixes: if I find a README typo or small lint fix, should I open a PR or push to main? also what's the preferred branch naming for first PRs? thanks!

Sam: always open a PR. we don't push directly to main. branch naming: `fix/jordan/readme-typo` or `chore/jordan/lint`. use kebab-case. include a short description. see CONTRIBUTING.md in the repo root.

Mira: yep PRs even for docs. for very small stuff we do squash+merge and add the label `size/tiny`. assign at least one reviewer (CODEOWNERS will auto-assign for some paths). if no obvious reviewer, ping #devex. also run pre-commit hooks locally.

Olivia: before you open, run the tests: `make test` and `./scripts/ci-local.sh`. CI runs linters & unit tests — fix those first. in your PR description include a brief "what/why" and link any related issue.

dev-bot: CI started for branch `fix/jordan/readme-typo` — status: queued

Jordan: awesome, thanks! small follow-up — what's our commit message style? conventional commits?

Sam: we prefer Conventional Commits but it's not strictly enforced. example: `fix(readme): correct typo in installation section`

Olivia: also add reviewers explicitly: @Sam for infra, @Olivia for docs if it's docs-heavy. add the `needs-review` label when ready.

ci-bot: CI passed ✅ all checks green.

Jordan: closing the loop — PR opened at https://github.com/redwood-inference/repo/pull/123 — thanks for the quick help :rocket:
